svg.title: Haar averaging and a change of section
svg.desc: Symbolic proof of Theorem 5.4. A sigma-finite measure M on K times F invariant under every left translation becomes m tensor kappa. Normalize a positive Haar density q and use p equals q times Delta, with m(Eh) equals Delta(h)m(E). The weighted label pushforward kappa is sigma-finite because finite-M cover slices u_n give kappa of u_n at least one over j bounded by j M(E_n). The affine example has left Haar da db over a squared and Delta(a,b) equals one over a. Replacing the section by (exp(z),0) times the old section changes the old coordinate to (a prime exp(z), b prime); its Jacobian is exp(z) and its label density is exp(-z). No numerical geometry is represented.
svg.text: Haar averaging recovers the product measure
Convention: m(Eh) = Δ(h)m(E); inversion density = Δ(h)⁻¹
On K × F, M is σ-finite.
m is a nonzero left Haar measure.
The result does not depend on q.
M(E_n) < ∞; the E_n cover K × F.
Nonnegative averaging — the exchanged factors are m and M
∫ f dM = ∫∫ p(g⁻¹h) f(h,z) dM(h,z) dm(g)
= ∫ q(h) [∫ f(k,z) dm(k)] dM(h,z) = ∫∫ f(k,z) dm(k) dκ(z)
κ is proved σ-finite by the slice cover; then M = m ⊗ κ. No conditional kernels are chosen.
Jacobian = eᶻ; a⁻² da db dz = (a′)⁻² da′ db′ e⁻ᶻ dz
dκ′(z) = Δ(eᶻ,0)dκ(z) = e⁻ᶻ dz; κ′ and κ have the same null sets.
This is a change of section at one fixed range unit; no field in the range unit is asserted.
Proof: Theorem 5.4, Proposition 5.6, Example 6.5. Haar prerequisites: Theorems 10.1 and 11.1.
